plain.text: Joseph presented five of his brothers to Pharaoh. They said they were shepherds and asked to live in Goshen, because the famine was severe in Canaan. Pharaoh told Joseph to settle his family in the best part of the land, Goshen, and to put capable men in charge of his own livestock. Joseph brought his father Jacob before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh. Pharaoh asked his age. Jacob said, "My years have been few and hard, 130 years; they do not equal the years of my fathers." Jacob blessed Pharaoh again and left. Joseph settled his family in the best land and provided them with food.

The famine was very severe, and there was no food anywhere. Joseph collected all the money in Egypt and Canaan in payment for grain and brought it to Pharaoh's palace. When the money ran out, the Egyptians gave their livestock for food. The next year they offered their land and themselves in exchange for food, and Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, except the priests' land. He gave the people seed and made it a law that a fifth of the harvest would belong to Pharaoh. The people said, "You have saved our lives."

The Israelites settled in Goshen, acquired property and grew greatly in number. Jacob lived in Egypt seventeen years and reached 147. When his death was near, he asked Joseph to promise not to bury him in Egypt, but with his fathers in Canaan. Joseph swore to do it, and Israel bowed in worship at the head of his bed.

summary.bigIdea: Jacob's family settles safely in Egypt, Joseph manages the famine, and Jacob asks to be buried in the promised land.
points: Pharaoh gives Jacob's family the best land in Goshen.
Jacob blesses Pharaoh and calls his own years "few and hard".
Joseph's policies keep Egypt alive; Jacob asks to be buried in Canaan.
summary.reflection: Jacob looked back on his life as "few and hard", yet he blessed others. How do you want to look back on your life?
